Poster_Title: The Unexplained Death of Francine Hunter: a Simulated Forensic Toxicology Scenario
Poster_Abstract: The final assessment for my Y3 Forensic Toxicology module centres around a simulated unexplained death scenario. Students work in small teams (~4) to review and analyse documentation, then request further information, analytical testing, and scientific data to try and determine cause of death. The activity was evaluated for the first time this year using the ASPECT tool as for the activity to successfully achieve its intended outcomes, many facets need to work in tandem, notably buy-in from both students and staff alike. The evaluation showed almost unanimously positive results for value of the activity, personal effort involved, and instructor contribution.

Poster_Title: Virtual chemistry experiments: Using thematic analysis to explore students lived experience
Poster_Abstract:
Virtual laboratories (VL) can provide students with learning experiences simulating practical experiments in a traditional laboratory. This study investigates students’ perspectives of the quality of their experiences learning in both traditional and VL; this is important as many settings are moving towards an expanded digital delivery.
This is a small-scale study of level 3 science students in a large Further Education college. Questionnaires and semi-structured interviews of students and staff were used to investigate learning in both traditional and VL. A thematic analysis was carried out – gaining insights into users’ views and experiences. 
Differences in experience between traditional and virtual laboratories were identified through themes of:- reality; control; skills; theory; truth and risk. The results of the study suggest that students have a richer and more fulfilling experience in a traditional laboratory, compared to the VL.

Poster_Title: Colourful Focus Groups for Evaluation and Data Collection
Poster_Abstract:
As part of our RSC Missing Elements funded project, we have designed and run student inter-led focus groups with small groups of students. Our goal is to evaluate our new chemistry specific study skills resources and to collect data such as advice from our students to create new resources.
We have designed our focus groups to include different ways of engaging with the topics under discussion to ensure the comfort of participants, essential as we aim for greater inclusion in research methods. By combining discussion (recorded via Microsoft Teams), coloured sticky notes and coloured pens, we can follow individual participant's contributions and enable withdrawal of consent/data afterwards. This poster is very much a work in progress: how we run our focus groups and the first results of analysis of the transcripts and other outputs.
If you are interested in accessing our resources to help support your own students, please get in touch. We will be creating a website to share them in Summer 2026.

Poster_Title: Triadic Conceptual Model for Optimizing STEM Education Through Science Museum Visits
Poster_Abstract:
This conceptual model demonstrates how Constructivism, Flow Theory, and
Autobiographical Memory function as mutually reinforcing cycles during museum
visits, creating optimal conditions for knowledge construction, deep engagement, and
personal meaning making for female STEM learners in resource constrained settings.

Poster_Title: Innovation: The Electrolysis of Water using Nitinol Wire Electrodes
Poster_Abstract: We have found that nitinol wire is an effective electrode for the electrolysis of water (1M Na₂SO₄ electrolyte), replacing the extremely expensive platinum wire used in previous microscale techniques. This brings green chemistry and principles associated with making the subject relevant to UNSDGs. The process uses modern materials and methods such as laser-cut acrylic plastic and a novel method of using 3-way taps and syringes to raise the electrolyte and remove gases for testing. The electrolyte contains bromothymol blue so that the acidic and alkaline nature of electrolysis can be seen. (In fact, putting a pH probe directly over the electrode wire records the extreme pH values.) The volume ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is the expected 2:1. We know that we can use inexpensive solar panels to carry out solar electrolysis of copper chloride solution, so the aim is to buy larger panels to produce green hydrogen from sunlight. Nitinol is familiar as a "memory metal" but not extensively used as an electrode. It might not be suitable as an industrial process, but this use is in education, illustrating to students possible solutions to climate change.
